messages:
Priya (eng-sec): starting a thread to capture UI + delegation concerns for operator RBAC migration. want to avoid surprises for tenant admins and keep audit surfaces clean.
Omar (platform): sweet. what's the primary UX surface this affects? console roles page + API key management endpoints?
Priya (eng-sec): yes. console roles, API key listing, and the operator settings page. plus CLI flows used by infra.
Yara (devx): most infra teams use the CLI and SDKs; if we change key shape we should offer transparent migration in SDKs. also add clear messaging in console.
Sam (sre): ops note: we need ability to emergency-revoke operator access across projects quickly. current model is manual and error-prone.
Priya (eng-sec): design goals: 1) least-privilege operator binding per-project, 2) clear visibility to tenant admins, 3) fast revocation paths, 4) low-friction migration.
Omar (platform): sketch options: A) per-project operator bindings shown in console (granular), B) global operator role with per-project allowlist (simpler UI), C) hidden service-to-project mapping with only audit logs (low surface).
Yara (devx): customers will want to see "which operators touched my project" in a simple list. option A best for trust.
Priya (eng-sec): tradeoffs: A increases UI complexity and storage for bindings; B easier but may confuse admins who expect to see per-project controls; C opaque is bad for compliance.
Sam (sre): revocation approaches: 1) revoke global operator key (blast radius big), 2) revoke project binding (good), 3) revoke specific token families (preferred). Need API + console affordances for all three.
Omar (platform): technical approach: introduce OperatorBinding entity: fields: operator_id, project_id, scopes (read/write/admin), created_by, created_at. Bridge and auth middleware consult binding service at token issuance time.
Priya (eng-sec): mapping to tokens: issue tokens with claims: op_id, binding_id, exp. downstream services can verify via JWT or check binding cache.
Yara (devx): console design: show Operator list -> per-operator card -> mapped projects with scope chips -> revoke button per binding -> bulk revoke. Add an "audit" drilldown showing recent actions.
Sam (sre): performance: binding lookups will be hot. propose a default cache TTL 60s with event-driven invalidation on binding changes. also keep a fast in-memory cache in auth middleware.
Priya (eng-sec): auditing: every binding create/update/revoke must emit an immutable audit event with actor, timestamp, reason, and request-id. store events in blob/ES for 365 days for compliance customers.
Omar (platform): migration plan idea: 1) export existing operator keys and map to inferred bindings (best-effort), 2) create bindings automatically but mark as "needs review" in console, 3) notify tenant admins with a migration checklist.
Yara (devx): add a one-click "review & approve mappings" flow for tenant admins to confirm inferred bindings. until approved, tokens still honor legacy model.
Priya (eng-sec): revocation edgecases: if an operator token is short-lived JWT, revocation during TTL needs introspection or a revocation list. propose short TTL (15m) + revocation stream for immediate cuts.
Sam (sre): operational SLOs: binding-service should have 99.95% availability, 99th latency < 200ms for cache misses. auth middleware must degrade to read cache + deny on catastrophic failure.
Omar (platform): telemetry: metrics we need: active bindings per operator, per-project operator call rate, binding creation/revocation rate, revocation latency from action->enforced.
Yara (devx): CLI shim: add "redwood auth migrate-ops" that runs preflight and shows missing bindings per project, plus an --auto flag to create bindings in draft state.
Priya (eng-sec): policy decision candidate: make per-project bindings visible by default for org admins; allow orgs to opt out to the "global operator mode" (for backward compatibility) for the migration window.
Sam (sre): fallback plan: support legacy keys for 120 days post-GA; add a hard alert when >0.5% of requests from a customer use legacy mode after 60 days.
Omar (platform): access model detail: binding scopes should be enumerated and small: deploy, read-config, manage-jobs, billing-read. keep it extensible but conservative.
Priya (eng-sec): security nit: require operators to have a registered signing key (KMS) and rotate keys quarterly. binding creation requires admin justification string in UI/CLI.
Yara (devx): UX microcopy: when creating binding ask: "Why does this operator need access?" and show affected projects. include link to audit policy.
Sam (sre): incident playbook notes: when a binding compromise suspected, steps: 1) revoke binding, 2) rotate operator signing key, 3) list affected runs and rollback if needed, 4) post-mortem. add playbook to runbook repo.
Omar (platform): open questions:
- should we include "expiration" on bindings (auto-expire) or force admins to renew?
- how to present binding inheritance for org-level operators?
- storage: SQL vs KV for bindings (transactions helpful).
Priya (eng-sec): my lean: include optional expiration (default 90d) with renewal reminders. inheritance: show inherited bindings but require explicit enable to escalate. storage: SQL (Postgres) for strong consistency and audit joins.
Yara (devx): timeline suggestion: week 0-2: backend schema + SDK shim; week 3: console UI beta + CLI preflight; week 4-6: internal canary; week 7: beta with opt-in customers; week 14: GA with 120d legacy support.
Sam (sre): i'll size infra and add paging for binding lists (some customers have many operators).
Omar (platform): I'll add DB schema PR and an API contract doc.
Priya (eng-sec): decision provisional: adopt per-project OperatorBinding with optional expiry, short-lived op tokens (15m) + revocation stream, default visible bindings in console, 120d legacy support window.
Yara (devx): lgtm from devx side.
Sam (sre): lgtm
Omar (platform): lgtm.
ops-bot: reminder: follow-up sync scheduled Tue 11:00 to review API contract and canary plan.
